label: second input step after a leading w (orig(0) = w, t = 1)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase and only when the previous input is w. Its main mode is t = 1 in sequences that start with w: it fires on every such step at near-max activation (0.85-1.0 of max) whatever the current token is, and this accounts for 93% of activation mass. It also fires weakly (about 0.02-0.3 of max, rarely higher) on some t = 2 steps where orig(1) = w, which is about 25% of active steps but only 7% of mass; about two thirds of those w-at-position-1 steps fire, including w w sequences. It never fires at t = 0, at later original positions, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, and never after any token other than w. A w-bigram detector restricted to the start of the sequence.

issues: The core predicate holds. On test, (t == 1) & (prev_tok == tok('w')) scores precision 1.0, recall 0.74, F1 0.850 and mass recall 0.926, with correlation 0.986. On dev there are 0 false positives. The feature is active only at t = 1 (93% of mass) and t = 2 (7%), and has zero activations at t = 0, t >= 3, on the delimiter and in the copy phase. All of that matches the explanation.

The explanation claims t = 2 firing includes 'w w' sequences. This is FALSE. (t == 2) & (prev_tok == w) & (orig(0) == w) gives precision 0.0 over 561 predicted steps on dev, so the feature never fires at t = 2 when the sequence starts with w w. All of the t = 2 activity comes from orig(0) != w.

The explanation claims it fires on 'about two thirds' of the t = 2 steps where orig(1) = w. This is FALSE. (t == 2) & (prev_tok == w) has precision 0.346 (5719 active out of 16511 steps), so about one third. Restricting to orig(0) != w only raises this to 0.359.

The t = 2 secondary mode depends partly on the first token: precision is 0.50 when orig(0) is a digit and 0.17 when it is a vowel. No clean rule was found, and adding it would not change F1 in any meaningful way, because the t = 2 mode is weak and holds only 7% of mass.

The other numbers check out: (t <= 2) & (prev_tok == w) gives recall 1.0, precision 0.676 and F1 0.807 (dev), and the misses show weak t = 2 activations of about 0.01-0.49. The label 'second input step after a leading w' matches the predicate and does not overclaim. The problem is two factual errors in the explanation's account of the secondary mode, not the label or predicate.
